divisions.question: That the amendments ( **Senator Cormann’s** ) be agreed to.

That consideration of the message in committee of the whole be made an order of the day for the next day of sitting. That the committee does not insist its amendments to which the House of Representatives has disagreed.

That so much of the standing and sessional orders be suspended as would prevent the Minister for Human Services moving an amendment to the Health Insurance Amendment (Compliance) Bill 2009 during the consideration of the Senate’s message insisting upon its amendments to the bill. That the House insists on disagreeing to amendments Nos 1 and 10 insisted on by the Senate. That the motion ( **Mr Bowen’s** ) be agreed to.

speeches.speaker: Anne McEwen
speeches.brief: The speaker moved that the bills proceed without formalities, be taken together and read a first time, and announced that after debate on the second reading is adjourned, one bill will be listed separately on the Notice Paper.

speeches.speaker: Anne McEwen
speeches.brief: The Health Insurance Amendment (Compliance) Bill 2009 was introduced to address the 20% of practitioners who refuse Medicare compliance audits, enabling document production and a 20% penalty on debts over $2,500, with audits limited to factual service elements and medical practitioner involvement. The Tax Laws Amendment (2009 Measures No. 2) Bill 2009 included extending small business CGT concessions, refundable tax offsets for the National Urban Water and Desalination Plan, and tax exemptions for Victorian bushfire clean-up grants.

speeches.speaker: Nigel Scullion
speeches.brief: The opposition moved amendments requiring Medicare Australia to consult professional bodies on audit documentation, to specify requested information in written notices, and to prevent the CEO from developing reasonable concerns about clinical relevance; they also moved to ensure disallowed Medicare items revert to previous regulations, which the Greens supported.

The House of Representatives agreed to Senate amendments (2) to (9) of the Health Insurance Amendment (Compliance) Bill 2009 but disagreed to amendments (1) and (10), requesting the Senate reconsider those two amendments.

speeches.speaker: Ursula Stephens
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the Health Insurance Amendment (Compliance) Bill 2009 should be dealt with immediately, criticizing Health Minister Nicola Roxon for a 50% cut to cataract surgery rebates and for refusing to table legal advice, and noted that the Senate had twice disallowed the cuts and passed a private member's bill to restore previous rebates.

speeches.speaker: Ursula Stephens
speeches.brief: The government adopted the committee report, arguing that opposition amendments (the cataract amendment and amendments 1 and 10) are unrelated to the Health Insurance Amendment (Compliance) Bill 2009 and constitute a political stunt, while the government supports only amendments arising from good-faith negotiations.
